title: Visual outcomes and complications of manual small-incision cataract surgery in patients with pseudoexfoliation

indication: Cataract with pseudoexfoliation (unilateral 28, bilateral 124 of 152 patients), age above 50 years; immature (nuclear sclerosis grade 2-3), mature, brown, hypermature and black cataracts and 2 phacolytic glaucoma; traumatic, congenital, complicated and uveitic cataract, corneal scars, previous ocular surgery, vision-impairing retinal pathology, uncontrolled systemic disease and monocular patients excluded

groups.description: Manual small-incision cataract surgery through a self-sealing sclerocorneal tunnel with PMMA IOL (bag or sulcus), single senior surgeon, intracameral adrenaline and moxifloxacin; pupil-expansion measures, CTR or anterior vitrectomy when needed; ofloxacin 2 weeks and tapering prednisolone acetate 6 weeks; hyperosmotic agent for stromal edema and anti-glaucoma treatment for epithelial edema

series.baseline_label: Preoperative CCT (Table 4 row 'Central corneal thickness in microns', column 'Preoperative Mean (SD) [Range]'); Topcon SP3000P specular microscope
series.notes: Table 4 columns Preoperative, 1 month, 3 months; cells are mean (SD) [range] and only the leading mean is read; per-visit n not tabulated

exclusions.what: Ranges in square brackets inside the Table 4 CCT cells
exclusions.reason: Ranges are not admissible; only the leading mean is read

exclusions.what: Table 4 rows 'Cell count', 'Cell Density Cells/mm2', 'Hexagonality in %' and 'Endothelial cell loss mean (percentage)'
Table 2 corneal edema and Descemet's fold counts at day 1, 1 week, 1 month and 3 months
exclusions.reason: Counts of clinical grades, not CCT values

notes: Prospective observational study, December 2016 to November 2017, 152 eyes of 152 patients, follow-up day 1, 1 week, 1 month and 3 months.
Role: single cohort defined by a patient condition (pseudoexfoliation) operated with standard MSICS; control.
Method: Table 4 lists CCT among the 'endothelial cell parameters noted on specular microscopy' (Results), measured with the Topcon SP3000P; recorded as 'specular'.
The article does not state whether the 7 eyes with intraoperative complications (zonular dialysis 5, posterior capsule rupture 1, iridodialysis 1) are included in Table 4.
Eyes with postoperative stromal or epithelial edema received additional hyperosmotic or anti-glaucoma treatment (Methods).
